scope: Isolated synthetic files and databases; no user library. Includes a 100MiB payload giant candidate. Not a real-book P95 or 60-minute soak.

checks: unannotated source rebuild performs one Worker scan, complete SHA-256 and metadata-only hot open
small, chapter and complete range recover atomically after insertion and preserve entity bodies/styles
renamed chapters recover only via both unique strong features plus an existing excerpt
deleted quote becomes invalid without overwriting original snapshot, quote or body
duplicate title and indistinguishable quotes stay pending, with no arbitrary chapter-index recovery
duplicate excerpts with unique exact context recover the correct new offset
reordered range endpoints and a missing endpoint never partially activate a range
unbound bindings are excluded; old referenced generations survive repeated cache GC
manual replacement while scanning wins binding epoch comparison and is never overwritten
entity edits during scanning are preserved while unchanged binding versions may recover
recovery SQL failure rolls back the index pointer, all binding updates and result rows
last-consumer close during candidate streaming cancels before publication and preserves old snapshots
source changes and active-generation CAS loss during recovery fail without binding writes
result pagination is bounded, stale versions disappear, backup retains recovered and pending snapshots
UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE BOM and GBK source changes preserve exact normalized quote offsets
100MiB giant candidate is streamed once in bounded decoded chunks and restores a deep emoji quote
additive recovery migration failure preserves existing formal rows and supports safe retry
relocation cannot silently override an available library original with a different selected file
relative offsets disambiguate duplicate context only under complete unchanged-source SHA-256 proof
unchanged-source proof preserves untitled fixed-chunk bindings without trusting generated chapter labels
TXT rebuilding never changes an existing non-TXT binding or its formal body
selected TXT exposes full validation/rebuild and original-source relocation in the existing annotations workspace
recovery summary remains stable after paint
UI rebuild restores a shifted binding and preserves formal body
UI rebuild validates complete SHA-256 without whole-source Renderer transfer
recovery result opens the original editor for manual binding and retained content
deleted excerpt keeps its body, quote and original location available for review
UI cancel preserves the published generation and annotations
actual Viewer offers original TXT relocation instead of a stale cache
relocation persists the existing book path through books.db without creating a new book
relocation keeps all formal annotation bodies attached to the original book key
relocated source reads actual current text through the bounded normal compiled reader
